#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR adds duration metrics for kubelet container probes.

```release-note
add container probe duration metrics
```

failures might be related. Something failing on probes initialization. Can it be the fact that we removed dimensions, would it break things when we copy dimensions?
@SergeyKanzhelev I assume you mean the removal of pod_uid?

> @SergeyKanzhelev I assume you mean the removal of pod_uid?

yes. It is just wild guess as failures started after this.
/retest
@SergeyKanzhelev re-added back `pod_uid` to attempt to sort of prove that the removal of it is the cause of test failures
/retest

Since @ehashman and @logicalhan also expressed some concerns with the current metric, could we perhaps resolve them before proceeding? https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104484/files#r750568110

From the slack discussion we had before the feature freeze (https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C20HH14P7/p1637080128045600), the most reasonable solution seems to be to remove the `pod_uid` label and prune the `uid` from the pod name before adding it to the `pod` label. For consistency, I think we should also apply these to the `probe_total` metric.

Bringing the original hold back, until we have addressed these points.
/hold
@dgrisonnet removing the `pod_uid` label produced broken test case outcomes. Not saying the concerns aren't valid, just FYI we haven't proven that removing the `pod_uid` is a functional change.

Since the metric is introduced by this PR, I wouldn't expect existing tests to depend on its `pod_uid` label, so it's weird to me that this could break test cases. Were you able to verify that the tests we failing because of this change or could it have been flakes?
@dgrisonnet I'm happy to make that change again and re-run tests. Shall I?
Yes, please. We can add this label to the metric since it would cause cardinality issues with ephemeral pods.

@dgrisonnet done with this commit: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104484/commits/344ed01a613c3a2da3f9bd80bfaaef5bffc28810

Current E2E jobs will tell the tale
Even though you removed the `pod_uid` label from the metric definition, you are still providing it when updating the metric which I suppose result in a fatal error.
@dgrisonnet good catch! fixed
/retest
@dgrisonnet @SergeyKanzhelev PTAL
this PR has been on hold for about 2 weeks. Can you please see how to unblock this by reviewing comments etc? or please close this out (Trying to declutter our open list of PRs)

Thx @dims

This comment still applies https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104484#issuecomment-989902194, we should remove the uid part of the pod name before proceeding with this PR.

issue_context.title: Create a duration metric for probes
issue_context.body:
/kind feature
/sig node

As exec probe timeout [bug was fixed](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1972), upgrade of k8s may lead to unexpected workload disruptions if the exec probe timeout is not corrected properly. Unfortunately there is no easy way today to guess which timeout should be set for the probe. The suggestion is to introduce a duration metric to allow customers to measure this time.

Likely here where other metrics are defined: /pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1972

/assign @jackfrancis
/cc @matthyx
